en: Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (*saraṇa*) and accompanied by rapture (*pītisahagata*), a state that is without-conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not accompanied by rapture arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*) ... three.
Dependent on a state that is without-conflict and accompanied by rapture, a state that is without-conflict and not accompanied by rapture arises by way of the root condition ...

one. Under the root condition there are four; under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two ... pe ... under the resultant condition (*vipāka*) there is one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are four.

Dependent on a state that is with conflict (*saraṇa*) and accompanied by pleasure, a state that is without conflict (*na-saraṇa*) and not accompanied by pleasure arises by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) … three.
Dependent on a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*) and accompanied by pleasure, a state that is without conflict and not accompanied by pleasure arises by way of root condition … one.

Under root condition there are four; under object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two … pe … under resultant condition (*vipāka*) there is one … pe … under non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are four.

Dependent on a state accompanied by equanimity that is a refuge, there arises a state that is not a refuge and not accompanied by equanimity, by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*)…. Under root condition there are four; under object condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two …pe… under result condition (*vipāka*) there is one …pe… under non-disappearance condition (*avigata*) there are four.
